football_evidence.question: Can San Diego State contain Fresno State’s explosive runs?
football_evidence.assessment: Some measured evidence supports EdgeDesk’s lean toward Fresno State, and its own breakdown accounts for about 0.0 of the 3.4 points, but not the full gap. It is a research question, not a bet.
supporting: When San Diego State has the ball (third down): San Diego State’s offense converts 23.8% of its third downs, and Fresno State’s defense allows opponents to convert 32.6% of their third downs (FBS average 39.5%).

When San Diego State has the ball (the passing game against the pass defense): San Diego State’s offense averages 5.2 yards per pass attempt, and Fresno State’s defense allows 7.0 yards per pass attempt (FBS average 7.5).

When San Diego State has the ball (big plays through the air): San Diego State’s offense turns 7.1% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and Fresno State’s defense gives up explosive gains on 7.6% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.4%).

When San Diego State has the ball (big plays on the ground): San Diego State’s offense turns 2.8% of its runs into explosive gains, and Fresno State’s defense gives up explosive gains on 5.8% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.6%).
contradicting: When Fresno State has the ball (big plays on the ground): Fresno State’s offense turns 9.3% of its runs into explosive gains, and San Diego State’s defense gives up explosive gains on 2.5% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.6%).
When Fresno State has the ball (the run game against the run defense): Fresno State’s offense averages 5.2 yards per carry, and San Diego State’s defense allows 4.5 yards per carry (FBS average 5.1).

When Fresno State has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): Fresno State’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 23.4% of its runs, and San Diego State’s defense stops 9.8% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.4%).
EdgeDesk’s position-group ratings put San Diego State’s offensive line No. 93 nationally and Fresno State’s No. 121.

Jayden Mandal has completed 110 of 173 passes (63.6%) for 1,252 yards, 7.2 yards per attempt, 8 touchdowns and 1 interception in six games for Fresno State, and has been sacked on 7 of 180 dropbacks.
